## What it is

Science builds on earlier science. Every researcher defers to published results they don't have time to check. That's necessary, but without systematic checking of the literature itself, meaning meta-science (replication, re-analysis, studying how research is done), deference becomes a trap. Errors in foundational papers spread into everything built on them, and nobody is in a position to notice.

## Why it matters

Each researcher's deference is individually rational: you can't re-derive every result you cite. Collectively, though, it means the reliability of a literature can be much lower than the reliability of any researcher's own work. Meta-science is how a field audits itself. Fields that dismiss it as "attacking science" are the ones most deeply in the trap.

## How it works

A toy model. Each new study builds on a few earlier ones. If any foundation is wrong, the new study's conclusion is compromised with some probability. Without checking, contamination accumulates over generations. With meta-science, a fraction of studies get checked, and when one is found wrong its descendants stop deferring to it. Contamination is then contained.

## Simulated example

Run 15 generations of a literature, with 100 studies per generation. Each builds on three earlier studies. Compare a field with no meta-science with one that checks a fraction of studies.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import {rng, range, mean, pct} from "../js/stats.js"
```

```{ojs}
viewof baseError = Inputs.range([0, 0.3], {value: 0.1, step: 0.01, label: "Chance a new study is wrong on its own"})
viewof inherit = Inputs.range([0, 1], {value: 0.4, step: 0.05, label: "Chance a wrong foundation compromises a study"})
viewof checkRate = Inputs.range([0, 0.5], {value: 0.2, step: 0.05, label: "Share of studies checked by meta-science"})
viewof seed = Inputs.range([1, 500], {value: 87, step: 1, label: "Random seed"})
```

```{ojs}
trap = {
  const r = rng(seed);
  const run = (check, label) => {
    let pool = range(100).map(() => ({wrong: r() < baseError, flagged: false}));
    const out = [{gen: 0, label, share: mean(pool.map(s => +s.wrong))}];
    for (let g = 1; g <= 15; g++) {
      pool.forEach(s => { if (check > 0 && s.wrong && r() < check) s.flagged = true; });
      const usable = pool.filter(s => !s.flagged);
      const next = range(100).map(() => {
        let wrong = r() < baseError;
        for (let k = 0; k < 3; k++) { const f = r.pick(usable.length ? usable : pool); if (f.wrong && r() < inherit) wrong = true; }
        return {wrong, flagged: false};
      });
      pool = [...pool.slice(-200), ...next];
      out.push({gen: g, label, share: mean(next.map(s => +s.wrong))});
    }
    return out;
  };
  return [...run(0, "No meta-science (pure deference)"), ...run(checkRate, "With meta-science checking")];
}
```

## R {.unlisted}

```{.r}
# Deference Trap: errors spread through a literature that never checks itself.
base_error <- 0.1 # chance a new study is wrong on its own # <1>
inherit <- 0.4 # chance a wrong foundation compromises a study
check_rate <- 0.2 # share of wrong studies caught by meta-science each round
set.seed(87) # <2>

run <- function(check) { # <3>
  wrong <- runif(100) < base_error
  flagged <- rep(FALSE, 100)
  share <- mean(wrong)
  for (g in 1:15) { # 15 generations of 100 studies
    flagged <- flagged | (wrong & runif(length(wrong)) < check) # <4>
    usable <- which(!flagged)
    if (length(usable) == 0) usable <- seq_along(wrong)
    new <- runif(100) < base_error
    for (k in 1:3) { # each new study builds on three earlier ones
      cited <- usable[sample.int(length(usable), 100, replace = TRUE)]
      new <- new | (wrong[cited] & runif(100) < inherit) # <5>
    }
    keep <- max(1, length(wrong) - 199):length(wrong) # the last 200
    wrong <- c(wrong[keep], new)
    flagged <- c(flagged[keep], rep(FALSE, 100))
    share <- c(share, mean(new))
  }
  share
}
deference <- run(0)
checked <- run(check_rate)

cat("Compromised after 15 generations: ", round(100 * tail(deference, 1)),
  "% with pure deference, ", round(100 * tail(checked, 1)),
  "% with meta-science checking\n",
  sep = ""
)

matplot(0:15, cbind(deference, checked), # <6>
  type = "l", lty = 1, lwd = 2,
  col = c("#d6604d", "#2166ac"), ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "Generation",
  ylab = "Share of new studies compromised"
)
legend("topleft", c("No meta-science", "With meta-science checking"),
  col = c("#d6604d", "#2166ac"), lwd = 2, bty = "n"
)
```
1. The page's controls: how often a new study is wrong on its own, how often a wrong foundation compromises a study that builds on it, and how much of the wrong work meta-science catches each round.
2. Fixes the random numbers so the run is reproducible.
3. Fifteen generations of 100 studies, with or without meta-science checking.
4. Checking: some of the wrong studies get flagged and are no longer built on.
5. Deference: each new study builds on three earlier ones and inherits their errors.
6. The share of new studies compromised, generation by generation.

## Python {.unlisted}

```{.python}
# Deference Trap: errors spread through a literature that never checks itself.
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

base_error = 0.1  # chance a new study is wrong on its own
inherit = 0.4     # chance a wrong foundation compromises a study
check_rate = 0.2  # share of wrong studies caught by meta-science each round
rng = np.random.default_rng(87)


def run(check):
    wrong = rng.uniform(size=100) < base_error
    flagged = np.zeros(100, dtype=bool)
    share = [wrong.mean()]
    for _ in range(15):      # 15 generations of 100 studies
        flagged |= wrong & (rng.uniform(size=wrong.size) < check)
        usable = np.flatnonzero(~flagged)
        if usable.size == 0:
            usable = np.arange(wrong.size)
        new = rng.uniform(size=100) < base_error
        for _ in range(3):   # each new study builds on three earlier ones
            cited = rng.choice(usable, 100)
            new |= wrong[cited] & (rng.uniform(size=100) < inherit)
        wrong = np.concatenate([wrong[-200:], new])  # keep the last 200
        flagged = np.concatenate([flagged[-200:], np.zeros(100, bool)])
        share.append(new.mean())
    return share


deference, checked = run(0), run(check_rate)
print(f"Compromised after 15 generations: {100 * deference[-1]:.0f}% with "
      f"pure deference, {100 * checked[-1]:.0f}% with meta-science checking")

plt.plot(deference, color="#d6604d", linewidth=2, label="No meta-science")
plt.plot(checked, color="#2166ac", linewidth=2,
         label="With meta-science checking")
plt.ylim(0, 1)
plt.xlabel("Generation")
plt.ylabel("Share of new studies compromised")
plt.legend()
plt.show()
```

## Key takeaways

::: takeaways
- Deference to the literature is necessary and, unchecked, dangerous.
- Errors spread through citation chains. Meta-science is how a field contains them.
- Replication and re-analysis are maintenance, not attacks.
:::
